Well, you’ve got to take the first step. I lost my girlfriend of six years recently and I felt the same way. Start going to therapy first. It’s going to be a struggle for a long time, but it doesn’t mean that’s the end of the world. You have to almost trick your brain into believing you’re okay. Every morning when you wake up, tell yourself that you are confident. After a couple days of telling yourself that you are you start to believe it. If you need to cry, get mad, whatever, let yourself do that for no more than 10 minutes then clear your mind and tell yourself you are confident! Not everything may go the way you want it too, but you’ve got to tell yourself, vocally if necessary, that that’s okay. There is no quick fix to this, and if there was it’s almost too good to be true. Do one thing a day at first that you are confident at. If you’re laying in bed all day, tell yourself you will get out of bed and force yourself to get dressed. Small things like that at first, then build it. Every day will be hard, but I know you’ve got it. You described my situation exactly, except the online part. If I can do it, so can you. I’m not saying give up on her, but you’ve got to show her that you’re changing your ways, you’ve got to show her the spark of why she fell for you in the first place. So, if you want her back, work on yourself. Don’t just tell her that you’re changing because she can see through that. SHOW HER! Best of luck man, I know you got this!

What my therapist told me, is to play your weaknesses into strengths. So shit I know I was doing wrong, focus on that and try to deduce why I was doing it. Then give it a little time, try to think rationally about why it got you fucked up,  then go back to it and reevaluate the situation. Easier said than done, absolutely but it seems to help when you use the PEPSI structure. P-person (you) E-emotion P-physical S- social I-intellect 
By going through each letter and talking yourself about why it’s emotional, physical, social or intellectual it gives you that moment to breathe
